clue.text: Heads of Daily Telegraph maintaining weird stain's removed

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the two capitals hold the rest between them
heads of means the first letters of the two newspaper words
weird signals that the letters of stain are reworked into an odd new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Bosses at a newspaper are seen protecting an odd-looking stain that has been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' sits at the end looking like part of the stain story, but it is the definition, meaning far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far off or remote can be described as removed, as in a cousin once removed.

clue.text: Dose working with pet at first, before it's put down

indicators.note: before means the earlier letters come ahead of the next word
working means the letters are being set in motion into a new order
at first means the first letter of pet

parts.note: it is taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet gives a pet a dose before it is put down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pet being put to sleep, but 'put down' simply means laid down, as money in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to set it down or lay it in place.

clue.text: Cusses terribly about Conservative victory

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters are placed around the abbreviation
terribly means the letters of cusses are badly rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician swears badly about a Conservative election win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes SUCESS from CUSSES, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Success is a triumph or favourable outcome, which a victory is.

clue.text: Permissible to remove large pants

indicators.note: to remove means the letter for large is taken away

parts.note: lawful means permitted or permissible
L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: It is allowed to take off big underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pants' means rubbish or very poor, not trousers or underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses pants as an adjective for something terrible, much like awful.

clue.text: Specialist catch with line at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An expert fisherman makes a catch with a line on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical describes specialised knowledge or terms belonging to an expert field.

clue.text: Company almost attempted to restrict European exclusive circle

indicators.note: to restrict means to hem in, so the shortened word closes round the letter
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: attempted means tried

explanation.surface: A firm nearly tried to keep a European out of its select group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TRIED to TRIE, and 'to restrict' puts E inside it to make TERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small select clique of people sharing interests, an exclusive social circle.

clue.text: Man's leggings

definitions.meaning: cowboys wear leather leggings over their trousers called by this name

explanation.surface: A man's leggings.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves for a fellow's possessive and for cowboy leather over-trousers.

clue.text: Criminal who stalks — they'll be seen on television

indicators.note: criminal signals the letters are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: A criminal stalker ends up on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Chat programmes with a host interviewing guests are broadcast on TV.

clue.text: Farmer finally runs with it inside sheep pen again

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of farmer
inside means the following letters go within the word for sheep

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer runs about inside a sheep pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like an enclosure for sheep but is the verb write, so 'pen again' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen is to write, so writing once more is to do it again.

clue.text: Perennial Dawson maybe planted in borders

indicators.note: planted in means put inside, like a plant in a bed

parts.note: ends are borders or edges
Les Dawson was a British comedian, so his first name is meant

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a perennial in the borders, maybe from Dawson's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Dawson was a well-known British TV comedian; 'Perennial' and 'borders' suggest gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting indefinitely or recurring, as everlasting does.

clue.text: Peaceful? Turning better if I start to complain

indicators.note: turning means the word for better is read backwards

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
taken as written

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of complain

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether getting better is peaceful if they begin to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes PAC from CAP, which means to better; the question mark marks the definition as a play on the ocean's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means calm or peace-loving, and the ocean was so named for its calm waters.

clue.text: Let everyone be indebted to daughter

parts.note: everyone means all
to be indebted is to owe
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent lets the whole family owe money to their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Let in the sense of permitted is a synonym, as in he was let in or permitted in.

clue.text: Baby plants bit of dad's heather with twigs around the outside

indicators.note: around the outside means the word for twigs encloses the other letters

parts.note: to twig is to understand or see, so twigs means sees

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of dad's

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A gardener describes young plants as part of father's heather, encircled by small twigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twigs' looks like plant matter but is the verb meaning understands, which wraps round the dad and heather pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedlings are young plants raised from seed, the infants of the garden.

clue.text: Hatred from goblin right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the word

parts.note: a sprite is a mischievous goblin or elf

explanation.surface: Someone feels hatred coming from a goblin who has suddenly left.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is malice or ill will, a petty form of hatred toward someone.

clue.text: Gallery frames second choice

indicators.note: frames means surrounds, as a picture frame surrounds a picture

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery hangs a picture in a frame as its second-best pick.
explanation.walkthrough: The TATE is a group of national art galleries in London; 'frames' fits the gallery picture but signals S going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one's preference or discernment, as in a choice of decor reflecting taste.

clue.text: Plots in Greene's novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
Greene's with the s counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A plot inside one of Graham Greene's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to contrive or scheme it into being.

clue.text: Cops and Morse drunk, getting Brahms and Liszt?

indicators.note: drunk signals the letters are jumbled, as if reeling about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV detective and his police colleagues get drunk, becoming 'Brahms and Liszt'.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for drunk (pissed), so the surface hangs together; Morse is a fictional Oxford detective. Here the two are simply examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms and Liszt were both nineteenth-century composers, so they are examples of the category.

clue.text: Soldier on ship eating fish spread

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the soldier word swallows the fish

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving on board ships
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A sailor on board eats fish on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: This butter substitute is spread on bread.

clue.text: Disorderly Irish soldier

parts.note: a regular is a professional soldier of a standing army

explanation.surface: An Irish soldier is behaving in an unruly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular means not following order or pattern, so disorderly or uneven.

clue.text: Tablet has no power with head ailment

indicators.note: has no means the letter for power is missing from the word

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: A pill with no strength is offered for a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks part of the ailment but means a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is a sickness or ailment.

clue.text: Go back and give someone another drink?

definitions.meaning: to go back or withdraw, as an army does
read as ..., to stand someone a drink again

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to the bar to buy another round.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawing is retreating, and treating again is split as re-treat.

clue.text: Dead reserved

definitions.meaning: a ... is slang for a corpse, and ... can mean dead and rigid
... also means formal and reserved in manner

explanation.surface: A body is described as dead and reserved.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a rigid corpse and a cool formal manner, as in a stiff greeting.

clue.text: Fancy Head of Intelligence cracked Enigma

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of intelligence
cracked means broken up, so the letters of enigma are rearranged

explanation.surface: The head of British intelligence cracked the Enigma code.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigma was the German wartime cipher machine cracked at Bletchley Park.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to picture or suppose it in the mind.

clue.text: What ships hold English in fear?

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is placed inside the word for fear

parts.note: fright is fear

explanation.surface: Asks whether ships hold Englishmen in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is cargo, which is carried in a ship's hold.

clue.text: Ready to follow the French language

indicators.note: to follow means the word for ready comes after the French article

parts.note: la is French for the, in the feminine
ready and tin are both slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared to learn a language after studying French.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready (as in ready cash) and TIN are both British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classical tongue of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Some feel a Borat episode's complicated and confusing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some viewers find an episode of the comedy Borat convoluted and baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate plan has many intricate parts, making it involved and hard to follow.

clue.text: Guard not opening mouth

indicators.note: not opening means without its first letter

parts.note: a sentry is a guard on watch

explanation.surface: A guard refuses to open his mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like opening the mouth but means the first letter of the guard word.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an entrance or opening, as the mouth of a cave is.

clue.text: Old, grim smell

parts.note: dour means stern and grim

explanation.surface: An old, grim smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, especially a distinctive one.

clue.text: Ecstasy left me in hospital department getting oxygen, say?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: in means the following word goes inside the department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug user collapses and is left in hospital, needing oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is one of the chemical elements, so it is an example; the question mark flags this.

clue.text: One runs about spilling gin — it's a job for the housekeeper?

definitions.text: it's a job for the housekeeper?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
on means about or concerning

indicators.note: spilling means the letters of gin are tipped out in a different order

explanation.surface: A housekeeper runs about after spilling gin, which is part of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes is a household chore that a housekeeper would typically do.

clue.text: Meet, perhaps, without shaking fist

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the word for perhaps surrounds the rest

parts.note: say means perhaps or for example

indicators.note: shaking means the letters of fist are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two people meet, perhaps without anyone shaking a fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense of outside, so the word for perhaps goes round the jumbled fist.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need or demand is to satisfy it.

clue.text: Determined to get money and set off

parts.note: to earn is to get money for work

indicators.note: off means the letters of set are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to make money and get going.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and resolute in intention.
